questions.stem: An elderly male with complaints of urinary retention was diagnosed with Prostate carcinoma. Gleason’s grading system is used for prognosis. The score is determined by evaluating which histological feature in prostate cancer.
questions.solutionHtml:
Architectural patterns
  • The Gleason score in prostate cancer is determined by evaluating the architectural patterns observed in the tumour tissue.
  • The higher the Gleason score, the more aggressive and poorly differentiated the prostate cancer cells are considered to be.
  • It helps in determining the prognosis and guiding treatment decisions for patients with prostate cancer. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 700

questions.stem: What is the normal upper limit of prostate-specific antigen for a 65 years old male?
questions.solutionHtml:
4.5 ng/mL
  • The normal upper limit of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) can vary depending on factors such as age, race, and individual characteristics.
  • However, a commonly used threshold for the normal upper limit of PSA in 65 years old men without prostate abnormalities is 5 ng/mL


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 700,701
